studies.label: Controlled crossover experiment: public transport and university-space ideation

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 16, Section 7, Limitations and Further Research; see also PDF p. 4, Section 4.1
counts_source.quote: The results of this research primarily derive from a cohort of 51 engineering students specializing in Industrial Design and Product Development.

arms.name: ChatGPT-assisted ideation
arms.description: Supervised ideation using ChatGPT on university-supplied computers; access to other websites and tools was restricted. Group B receives this condition for the public-transport task and Group A for the university-spaces task. These labels refer to current assistance conditions, not independent parallel groups across both tasks (PDF pp. 6-7, Section 4.3.1 and Figure 1).

arms.name: Unaided ideation
arms.description: Supervised ideation in a computer-free classroom without external support tools. Group A receives this condition first and Group B receives it after its earlier ChatGPT-assisted task (PDF pp. 6-7, Section 4.3.1 and Figure 1).

studies.country: Spain (study institution; PDF p. 1 affiliations and PDF p. 4, Section 4.1). Participant nationality is not stated.
studies.task: Third-year industrial design and product development engineering students generated innovative ideas to improve public transport and university spaces, each as a sketch and brief description, with eight unique ideas requested within 30 minutes per task (PDF p. 6, Section 4.3.1).

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT (GPT-3.5)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 7, Section 4.3.1; the model is named, but its release year and the data-collection year are not stated.

preregistration.where: No preregistration or registration reference is stated in the complete paper.

studies.shared_sample: Possible shared sample with c031, Evaluating AI-assisted creative ideation: A crossover study in higher education (DOI 10.1016/j.tsc.2025.101958), as flagged in forms/c201.json sample_overlap. Matching cohort, design and idea counts suggest overlap, but participant identity is unconfirmed. No c031 statistics are used here.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Anonymous peer ratings by participating third-year students, excluding self-evaluation. Agreement scale from 1 (Strongly Disagree) to 4 (Strongly Agree). Items: Is creative; Solves the problem in an original way; Is unconventional. Instrument: PDF p. 5, Section 4.2.1 and Table 1; rating procedure: PDF p. 8, Section 4.3.2.

sources.locator: PDF p. 7, Table 3, Subtotal row, Task 1: public transport column
sources.quote: Subtotal 353 375 728

sources.locator: PDF p. 11, Figure 7, Task 1: public transport panel
sources.quote: Results of the evaluation of the ideas obtained. scale: From 1 to 4.

sources.locator: PDF p. 9, Section 5, paragraph describing the randomized assistance comparison
sources.quote: the Mann–Whitney test showed no significant differences between ideas generated with the help of ChatGPT and those generated without assistance.

sources.locator: PDF p. 5, Section 4.2.1; Table 1 defines the outcome items
sources.quote: A Likert scale ranging from 1 (Strongly Disagree) to 4 (Strongly Agree) was employed to evaluate each criterion for every idea.

estimates.notes: Figure 7 presents this contrast only as bars with error bars. No exact arm means, SDs, SEs, differences, confidence limits, test values, p-values or standardized effects are printed. No bar heights or error-bar lengths were digitized. The narrative reports no significant assistance-versus-unaided differences using the Mann-Whitney test, but does not provide the statistics; test and p_value therefore remain null. The type and unit of the plotted uncertainty are undefined, and pairing, participant clustering, and aggregation across raters are not described; se_basis is unclear. n_units records the printed idea-corpus count, not the number of ratings or a separately reported outcome-specific complete-case count. The later session rated previously generated ideas; it was not a delayed creative-production task. First-round comparison between the randomized sequences: Group B used ChatGPT and Group A worked unaided. The task was completed before the experimental crossover. A task-specific participant analysis count and the numbers of people in the two sequences are not printed.
